s1.quote: Northern Arch, located at the northern end of Puketuaho Island … it is susceptible to current … At 40m in the middle, the bouldery bottom tumbles away to beyond 50m at either end.

s2.quote: The bottom of the arch is at 125 feet (38 m)

s3.quote: Northern Arch: If you enjoy deep diving and big fish, then this is the dive site for you.

highlights.text: Huge snapper and kingfish in the current

summary.text: A short, narrow archway at the northern tip of the Poor Knights whose boulder floor drops to about 40 m and beyond. Current pours through and feeds sponge-covered walls, big schools of maomao, snapper, kingfish and seasonal stingrays.

s1.quote: Middle Arch is another impressive dive site, suitable to all experience level. The bottom of the arch sits at around 16m, however the bay out from the arch, drops to an insane 80m!

s2.quote: Middle Arch … normally with less current that Northern Arch. Blue Maomao and Two Spot Demoiselles usually dominate the site

hazards.text: Bay beside the arch drops to about 80 m

s1.quote: Keen on Macro photography , then Magic Wall is a great hangout for you. … Loads of Nudibranch species, both big and small, can be found along the wall and keep your eyes peeled for Moray Eels

highlights.text: Moray eels draped over sponges and kelp

s1.quote: Often chosen as a dive site for beginner divers The Gardens shouldn’t be underestimated. The Gardens is home to a number of juvenile fish. Close to the cliffs the depths range from 5m to 10m

s2.quote: The Cream Gardens, this dive site isn’t one of the most well-known sites but is equally impressive.

highlights.text: Juvenile fish, snapper, angelfish, eagle rays

s1.quote: Blue Maomao Arch is probably one of the most popular and photographed dive sites at the Poor Knights.  Ideal for snorkelers and divers, situated in the Labrid Channel

s2.quote: Blue Maomao Arch , probably the most famous and popular of the arches is a shallow arch with a window that allows a light beam in at certain points of the day.

highlights.text: Shafts of sunlight through the arch

summary.text: The most photographed arch at the Poor Knights: a shallow, low-lying arch where light beams stream in through gaps in the rock above dense schools of blue maomao. Suits snorkellers and relaxed dives.

s1.quote: Maomao Arch cuts through Tawhiti Rahi, allowing snorkelers and divers to cross through when the sea conditions allow.

s2.quote: Blue Maomao arch and have a relaxing shallow cave dive

access.value: Passage through the arch depends on sea conditions

s1.quote: Rikoriko Cave is the largest sea cave (by volume) in the southern hemisphere. Most dive charters will take boats into the cave

s2.quote: Rikoriko Cave is the flagship of the Poor Knights, reputedly the largest sea cave in the world … it would be unwise to surface in mid water.

highlights.text: Largest sea cave by volume in the southern hemisphere

hazards.text: Boat traffic - do not surface in mid water

sites.name: Trevor’s Rocks

s1.quote: Trev's Rock joins a wall beginning at 20m depth and reaching the sand at 30m … Trev's Rock is a boating hazard and must be approached with care, particularly at low spring tide.

hazards.text: Boating hazard at low spring tide

sites.depthNote: Shallow side ~10 m; wall 20-30 m (Trev's Rock)

s1.quote: It is not uncommon to find 3-11 large stingrays there … The Labyrinth is an underwater ridge descending from the surface down to the sand at 25m

highlights.text: Labyrinth ridge: night diving, cracks and tears

s1.quote: This is a popular site for all dive levels … You will do a shore entry from the beach … You will not find much more than 4m depth for about the first 300m off the beach.

s2.quote: The marine reserve offers some of the best snorkelling and scuba diving opportunities close to Auckland.

s3.quote: Goat Island Channel is not deep (between 2 and 5 m)

access.value: Marine reserve - no fishing or taking marine life

hazards.text: Unsafe in E/NE winds over 20 kn or swells over 1 m

s1.quote: As you get past Shag Rock (this is the out crop of rock that is just covered at high tide, off the corner of the island) you will slowly start to gain depth.

s2.quote: Shag Rock breaks the monotony of the area, offering hiding places for fish and crayfish

highlights.text: Hiding places for fish and crayfish

hazards.text: Rock is awash and covered at high tide

s1.quote: 30 minutes from Dive Now, Whangarei is this fantastic shore dive. Average depth of 5m with a max of 12m at the mouth of the bay. Fingers of encrusted reef run along the edge of the bay … Leather jackets, Blennies, Red Moki, Goat fish and baby snapper are common to see during the day.

highlights.text: Leatherjackets, red moki, goatfish, baby snapper
